scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of the default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. Jupyter .ipynb files (47) were treated as Python; embedded base64 image outputs in notebooks were ignored. The repo is a collection of tutorial scripts and notebooks; there is no application server, so interfaces are limited to script entry points. Severity judgement: the same MySQL password for user 'jcz' is hardcoded in 19 places (tracked files), pointing at localhost or a private LAN address (192.168.1.110); rated critical per skill rules (live-looking DB credential committed to a tracked file), although reachability is limited to the author's network. One placeholder template URL in pandas/21_sql/pandas_sql.ipynb is rated low; the same notebook also uses a root user with an empty password on localhost (not recorded as a secret). Scope: matpltlib/ and Basics/ contain Windows-style hardcoded paths in tutorial code.

gitignore_gaps: tracked binary data files exist despite a comprehensive Python .gitignore: matpltlib/map_data.db, population.db, population_orig.db, weather.4Sept2019.db.zip, data.csv, petals.xlsx and several weather*.csv

db.sqlite3 and .env are ignored; *.db is not ignored

what_this_app_can_do: Reads weather, gas and electric-utility views from a MySQL 'weather' database on localhost or 192.168.1.110 using a hardcoded username and password, and plots them as charts saved to PNG files.
Reads local CSV, Excel and SQLite files and plots or prints the contents (tutorial examples).
Fetches the Matplotlib release list from the public GitHub API to draw a timeline chart.
Includes tutorial notebooks and scripts for pandas, matplotlib, bokeh, and Python basics; some write to hardcoded C:\ paths.

data_sources_touched.source: MySQL 'application' database on localhost (root, empty password) in a tutorial notebook
CSV and Excel files in the repo (data.csv, petals.xlsx, weather*.csv)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Nothing is served: scripts run only for whoever executes them locally and connect out to a local or private-LAN MySQL server. Because the repo is on GitHub, the hardcoded database credentials are visible to anyone who can read the repository.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Same MySQL password for user 'jcz' hardcoded in 19 tracked files (scripts and notebooks), including a private LAN host address
Hardcoded Windows paths (C:\data, C:\Code) in tutorial code
Binary database and data files (.db, .xlsx, .csv, .zip) committed to the repo

top_findings: Hardcoded MySQL password (user jcz) repeated across 15 tracked scripts and notebooks (19 occurrences)
No dependency manifest despite pandas, matplotlib, sqlalchemy, numpy usage
Committed binary data files (SQLite .db, xlsx, csv, zip)
